description: Arelle is an open-source platform for validating, exploring and extracting data from XBRL and inline XBRL financial reports. It runs as a desktop application on Windows, macOS and Linux, a command line tool, a Docker image, a Python API, a plugin system and a local web server, and checks filings against specifications and the filing rules of regulators such as ESMA's European Single Electronic Format, SEC EDGAR, the US Federal Energy Regulatory Commission, Japan's EDINET, South Africa's CIPC, the Netherlands, the UK's HMRC and Ireland's Revenue. It has been maintained in the open since 2010, with the site copyright held by Workiva, and says more than 100 regulators, banks and technology firms rely on it. It is global. The software is free; the package on PyPI, arelle-release version 2.45.3 of 24 September 2026, is licensed Apache-2.0 and needs Python 3.10 or later. Caveats: it validates and extracts reported facts but does not supply the filings or clean economic series, and rule packs vary by regulator. For simulation it prepares structured financial statements of listed utilities, banks and industrial firms, for example as balance sheet inputs to financial resilience and contagion models. It is related to the XBRL business reporting standard record in this catalogue, the format it processes.
